message.content: They say that he controlled the Nile, but they know it was trade that truly empowered him. She argued that her kingdom relied on foreign goods, yet he insisted that their wealth came from within. We see that his power grew because they exchanged gold for grain. You might think that only armies mattered, but we know that merchants built their influence. The scribes wrote about these deals, and they recorded every ounce of incense. He demanded tribute, so she sent slaves, and they accepted the payment gladly. If you ask why he ruled so long, we must look at their networks. They connected distant lands, so he could claim them as his own. We believe that this system made his reign stable, while others feared its reach.
